title: Writing custom rule tables
text: rules table needs exactly two columns: flag_name: unique label per rule. Can use ISCN-style punctuation readability (e.g. "t(9;22)(q34;q11)") – output column sanitized version, runs non-alphanumeric characters replaced _. regex: pattern matched token. Rules fire independently – ’s priority ranking , two patterns can match flag, combine one regex | rather using two rows. output column (t_X_18_p11_q11) free characters ((, ), ;) otherwise force backtick-quoting (r$`t(X;18)(p11;q11)`) interactive use.
code: my_rules <- validate_rules(tibble::tibble(   flag_name = "t(X;18)(p11;q11)",   regex = "t\\(X;18\\)\\(p11;q11\\)|t\\(18;X\\)\\(q11;p11\\)" )) my_rules #> # A tibble: 1 × 2 #>   flag_name        regex                                               #> * <chr>            <chr>                                               #> 1 t(X;18)(p11;q11) "t\\(X;18\\)\\(p11;q11\\)|t\\(18;X\\)\\(q11;p11\\)"  result <- parse_karyo(   "46,XX,t(X;18)(p11;q11)",   rules = my_rules,   on_issues = "warn",   verbose = FALSE ) result |>   dplyr::select(t_X_18_p11_q11, general_translocation) #> # A tibble: 1 × 2 #>   t_X_18_p11_q11 general_translocation #>            <int>                 <int> #> 1              1                     1

title: Writing custom rule tables
text: validate_rules() rejects duplicate flag_name values – one maps exactly one output column: also rejects distinct flag_name values collide sanitized column name, even though raw names differ:
code: validate_rules(tibble::tibble(   flag_name = c("del(5q)", "del(5q)"),   regex = c("del\\(5q", "del\\(5\\)\\(q") )) #> Error: #> ! `rules` has duplicate `flag_name` value(s): del(5q). Each flag_name must map to exactly one rule -- combine alternative patterns into a single regex instead. validate_rules(tibble::tibble(   flag_name = c("t(9;22)", "t(9,22)"),   regex = c("t\\(9;22\\)", "t\\(9;22\\)") )) #> Error: #> ! `rules` has `flag_name` value(s) that collide once sanitized into an output column name: t(9;22), t(9,22). Rename one of the conflicting flag_name values so they remain distinct after stripping non-alphanumeric characters.

title: Writing custom rule tables
text: parse_karyo()’s rules argument also accepts list() karyo_rules tables, combining flags: flag_name must stay unique across combined tables – ’s cross-table priority resolve clash, combining two tables define, say, "shared_flag" errors instead silently keeping one:
code: lesion_a <- validate_rules(tibble::tibble(   flag_name = "flagA",   regex = "t\\(9;22\\)\\(q34;q11\\)" )) lesion_b <- validate_rules(tibble::tibble(   flag_name = "flagB",   regex = "del\\(5\\)\\(q13q33\\)" ))  result <- parse_karyo(   c("46,XX,t(9;22)(q34;q11)", "46,XX,del(5)(q13q33)"),   rules = list(myeloid_rules, lesion_a, lesion_b),   on_issues = "warn",   verbose = FALSE ) result |>   dplyr::select(t_9_22_q34_q11, flagA, flagB) #> # A tibble: 2 × 3 #>   t_9_22_q34_q11 flagA flagB #>            <int> <int> <int> #> 1              1     1     0 #> 2              0     0     1 set_a <- validate_rules(tibble::tibble(   flag_name = "shared_flag",   regex = "t\\(9;22\\)\\(q34;q11\\)" )) set_b <- validate_rules(tibble::tibble(   flag_name = "shared_flag",   regex = "del\\(5\\)\\(q13q33\\)" )) parse_karyo(   "46,XX,t(9;22)(q34;q11)",   rules = list(set_a, set_b),   on_issues = "warn",   verbose = FALSE ) #> Error: #> ! `rules` has duplicate `flag_name` value(s): shared_flag. Each flag_name must map to exactly one rule -- combine alternative patterns into a single regex instead.

title: Cleaning dirty karyotype strings
text: Every issue check_karyo() finds either fixable (formatting artifact) unfixable (structural problem). preprocess_karyo() touches fixable kind – unfixable rows always come NA, matter on_issues mode use. Columns karyotype/fixable/unfixable one 0/1 flag per unfixable issue type (alphabetical). Fixable issue types don’t get columns – preprocess_karyo() resolves automatically, row simply flagged fixable, without needing know specific fixable pattern fired. full catalog issue types, whether surface column: Fixable: chimeric_separator, count_sex_separator (e.g. 46XY 45.XY missing comma sex complement), embedded_newline, fish_notation, fullwidth_punctuation (fullwidth brackets, tilde, parentheses, comma, semicolon, equals sign standing ASCII equivalents), html_entities, leading_dot, mar_space, midstring_linewrap, missing_sex_comma (e.g. 46,XX der(...) 46,XY+8 missing comma sex complement – letter-glued form like 46,XYdel(5q) auto-fixed glued token recognized aberration indicator, otherwise ’s detected comes back NA), non_ascii_homoglyph (Greek Chi/Upsilon standing Latin X/Y sex complement), non_clonal_sca (ncSCA token, standalone parenthesized), trailing_narrative, unicode_notation, zero_host_chimera. Unfixable: constitutional_sex_complement, empty, invalid_idem, mosaic_karyotype, multiple_chimeric_separator, no_chromosome_count, no_sex_complement, single_token, stray_non_ascii, unbalanced_brackets, unbalanced_parentheses, unparseable_bracket, updated_iscn.
code: ck <- check_karyo(example_karyotypes, karyotype_column = "karyotype") names(ck) #>  [1] "karyotype"                     "fixable"                       #>  [3] "unfixable"                     "constitutional_sex_complement" #>  [5] "empty"                         "invalid_idem"                  #>  [7] "mosaic_karyotype"              "multiple_chimeric_separator"   #>  [9] "no_chromosome_count"           "no_sex_complement"             #> [11] "single_token"                  "stray_non_ascii"               #> [13] "unbalanced_brackets"           "unbalanced_parentheses"        #> [15] "unparseable_bracket"           "updated_iscn"

title: Cleaning dirty karyotype strings
text: preprocess_karyo() function rewrites string. applies fixes fixed order, final normalize_iscn() pass: Trim leading/trailing whitespace Replace unicode spaces (NBSP), zero-width spaces, dashes (em/en-dash), fullwidth +/- characters Normalize Greek letter homoglyphs (Chi/Upsilon) Latin X/Y sex chromosome complement Replace fullwidth ISCN punctuation (brackets, tilde, parentheses, comma, semicolon, equals sign) ASCII equivalents Collapse embedded newlines/tabs spaces Decode HTML entities (< -> <, > -> >, & -> &) Strip leading dot(s) digit (e.g. .46,XX -> 46,XX) Insert missing/dotted separator chromosome count sex complement (e.g. 46XY 45.XY -> 46,XY/45,XY) Strip FISH/nuc ish annotation (suffix mid-clone metaphase count) Strip trailing narrative: ] .text -> ]; ) Capital text -> ) Collapse mid-string line-wrap artifacts (, .der(...) -> ,der(...)) Insert missing comma sex chromosome complement Remove space count mar token (+1~4 mar -> +1~4mar) Strip non-clonal single-cell abnormality (ncSCA) tokens, standalone parenthesized normalize_iscn(): whitespace collapsing, delimiter tightening, idem/sl/cp normalization (zero_host_chimera chimeric clone selection happen alongside pipeline covered separately vignette("chimeric-karyotypes").) preprocess_karyo() accepts karyo_check object directly (returned check_karyo()), reusing cached assessment instead re-scanning:

title: Getting started with karyoparser
text: check_karyo(), preprocess_karyo(), parse_karyo() one job, none need others – call whichever one actually need. first time ’re working new dataset, though, run three order – diagnose, clean, extract – actually see ’s wrong data quietly turns missing rows. check_karyo() – diagnose. Read-. Scans input returns karyo_check tibble flagging issue types (dirty markers, chimeric separators, structural errors), plus fixable/unfixable summary columns. preprocess_karyo() – clean. function rewrites string. Fixes ’s fixable returns narrow karyo_preprocessed tibble (original, preprocessed, status). parse_karyo() – extract. Feature extraction – cleaning . on_issues = "preprocess" can invoke check/fix logic internally, single call often enough; chain three explicitly also want diagnostic cleaned tibble right. See vignette("data-cleaning") full on_issues reference.

Fixable rows formatting artifacts (stray whitespace, HTML entities, missing comma, …); unfixable rows structural problems (chromosome count, mosaicism, …) always come NA. preprocess_karyo() touches fixable kind. title: Getting started with karyoparser
text: Every flag 0 1, every flag fires independently – ’s priority competition , one token can light several flags . come three sources: Specific rule flags – one per myeloid_rules entry, fired regex matches token (e.g. t(9;22)(q34;q11), del(5q)). General structural flags (general_*) – universal, disease-agnostic detections (translocation, deletion, inversion, addition, dicentric, isodicentric, pseudodicentric, isochromosome, ring, insertion, duplication, triplication, marker, double minutes, derivative). Always , regardless rule set pass. Aneuploidy flags (mono*/tris*) – whole-chromosome loss/gain -/+ tokens. Since flags don’t compete, token can trip matches . t(9;11)(p21;q23) sets specific t_9_11_p21_q23, family flag t_v_11q23, general_translocation; del(5q) sets del_5q general_deletion. Family detectors (t_v_11q23, t_v_11p15, t_3q26_v, t_5q, t_12p) deliberately co-fire specific flags – mean “rearrangement involving region/arm”. *_other variants (e.g. t_9_22_other) complement canonical breakpoints: fire chromosome pair non-canonical breakpoints – exclusion lives regex , canonical token sets just specific flag.
